1. Miscellaneous Appeal No.632/2016 has been preferred by the appellant/Insurance Company challenging the award dated 30.04.2016 passed by the Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Gwalior (M.P.) in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4550 2 MA-632-2016 Claim Case No.114/2014 on the ground of exoneration from liability.
Miscellaneous Appeal No.767/2016 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants challenging the same award on the ground of enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: Since both the appeals arise out of the same award and involve common facts and issues, they were heard analogously and are being decided by this common judgment.
3. The date of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle and negligence are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality.
The dispute pertains to the liability of the Insurance Company and quantum of compensation.

4. As per findings of the Claims Tribunal, in the case of death of Mahendra Singh Kushwah in motor accident, an amount of compensation to the tune of Rs.8,45,000/- has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal with interest from filing of claim petition till its realization.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company in MA No.632/2016 submitted that the impugned award is contrary to the facts, evidence on record and settled principles of law.

It was contended that the Claims Tribunal itself recorded a finding that the offending dumper bearing No.
MP-07-HB-0476 was being driven without a valid and effective fitness certificate on the date of accident, which amounts to breach of policy conditions.

It was further submitted that as per the statement of the R.T.O. official and Section 56 of the Motor Vehicles Act, a vehicle cannot be plied NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4550 3 MA-632-2016 without a valid fitness certificate and on its expiry, the permit and registration are deemed cancelled.
Despite this, the Claims Tribunal wrongly fastened liability upon the Insurance Company.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents opposed the aforesaid submissions and prayed for dismissal of MA No.632/2016.
7. In MA No.767/2016, learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submitted that the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is on the lower side.

It was argued that despite clear oral and documentary evidence showing that the deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month as a tutor, the Tribunal arbitrarily assessed the income at Rs.5,000/- per month.

It was further contended that considering the educational qualifications and future prospects of the deceased, the income ought to have been assessed at a higher figure and that the compensation awarded under conventional heads is also inadequate.
Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned award.
8. Learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company opposed the submissions made on behalf of the appellants/claimants and prayed for dismissal of MA No.767/2016.

9. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
Adjudication of MA No.632/2016 (filed by Insurance Company)
10.
From perusal of the record, it is evident that the deceased was a third party.

It is also undisputed that on the date of accident, the offending NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4550 4 MA-632-2016 vehicle did not possess a valid and effective fitness certificate, which amounts to breach of the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy.
However, since the deceased was a third party, the Insurance Company cannot be exonerated from liability altogether.

In view of settled law,
The New India Insurance Company Limited ... vs Smt. Rajeshwari Kushwah on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72445562/
2 the Insurance Company is liable to satisfy the award with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
11.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the finding of the Claims Tribunal fastening absolute liability upon the Insurance Company is modified to the extent that the Insurance Company shall pay the compensation to the claimants with liberty to recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
12. In view of the above, MA No.632/2016 is partly disposed of.

Assessment of compensation in MA No. 767/2016 (filed by claimants)
13.

So far as enhancement of compensation is concerned, the Claims Tribunal itself held that mark sheets from Exhibit P-12 to Exhibit P-20 relating to High School, Higher Secondary, Graduation and DCA (Computer Course) etc of the deceased are genuine and duly proved.
The Tribunal also observed that the deceased was an educated and married person and could not have been sitting idle.

In such circumstances, when documentary proof of exact income is not available, the income is required to be assessed in accordance with the Minimum Wages Act, as held in Sukhdevi v.
Devendra Kumar, ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways , 2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi , (2008) 3 ACC 134 .

Accordingly, the monthly income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.5,800/- per month as per the Minimum Wages Act.

14. As regard to loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects.

Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 , even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of 18 has rightly been applied by the Claims Tribunal.

After deducting Dependency 1/3 Rs.64960/-
 Multiplier 18 Rs.1169280/-
 Other Heads:-
 Loss of Consortium Rs.40,000 X 4 = Rs  Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
Total = Rs.13,59,2

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in MA No.767/2016 is Rs.13,59,280/- as against the sum of Rs.8,45,000/- awarded by NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4550 6 MA-632-2016 the learned Claims Tribunal.
Accordingly, the appellants/claimants in MA No.767/2016 are held entitled to an additional compensation of Rs.5,14,280/- over and above the amount already awarded by the Tribunal.
17. Consequently, MA No. 767/2016 is partly allowed, and the compensation amount is enhanced by Rs.5,14,280/-.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the same rate as awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall be paid to the claimants within a period of three months from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
The remaining conditions imposed by the learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

18. In case the enhanced compensation exceeds the valuation of MA No.767/2016, the claimants shall deposit the differential Court fee (if not already paid) within a period of one month from today and furnish proof of such payment before the Registry.
Upon compliance, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of this order.
19. In view of the foregoing discussion, MA No.767/2016 filed by the appellants stands disposed of accordingly.

20. Let a copy of this order be kept in other connected matter.
